title: The Salvadoran Jesuits (1989)
hookLine: six Jesuits and two women killed at a university in San Salvador

lines: A CAMPUS IN A CIVIL WAR.
cards: A university campus in San Salvador, during a civil war. You met Oscar Romero earlier on this path; this is his country. The Jesuits who run the university live in a house on the grounds.
They are professors: a philosopher, a psychologist, a sociologist, theologians, and an older priest who works with schools for the poor.
A woman named Elba Ramos cooks and keeps house for them, and on this night she and her daughter Celina are sleeping there, in a room of the house. Before dawn, soldiers come through the gate.
Today, stay with them quietly, and ask what kind of teaching gets a person killed.

teach.b: The Salvadoran Jesuits. That night, soldiers of the Salvadoran army killed six Jesuit priests at the Central American University, along with Elba and Celina Ramos.
A United Nations truth commission later investigated and named the military as responsible. The rector was Ignacio Ellacuría, a philosopher.
With him died Ignacio Martín-Baró, a psychologist; Segundo Montes, a sociologist; Amando López; Juan Ramón Moreno; and Joaquín López y López. Why them?

They carried no weapons. They carried research, lectures and public arguments. Their university had spoken out about the poor and the suffering of ordinary people in the war, and it had pressed for a negotiated peace.
For some in power, that teaching was dangerous. Here the last few days come home.

teach.h: THE WHOLE PERSON, A WHOLE PEOPLE.
teach.b: Cura personalis, the whole person, stretched to a whole people. God in all things, including a country's poorest neighborhoods. The magis, asking what a university is for.
These men had decided the answer included telling the truth out loud.

teach.h: ELBA AND CELINA, NOT ONLY THE Well-known.
teach.b: And Elba and Celina are a reminder that the dead were not only the well-known ones.

teach.h: GREATER LOVE THAN THIS NO MAN HATH.
teach.b: In John's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus says: "Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life for his friends." Today, people come to the campus to pray where they died. The point is not drama.
It's that teaching matters, and telling the truth in a classroom can cost something, in some places still.

how: Catholics, and especially Jesuit schools and universities, remember the Salvadoran Jesuits and Elba and Celina Ramos with Masses, vigils and prayers for peace and justice.

games.q: you run a university in a country at war. speaking about the poor and calling for peace could put you in danger. what do you do?
o: keep quiet and teach only safe subjects.
keep teaching and speaking the truth about the poor.
close the university until the war ends.
games.why: the UCA Jesuits kept speaking and teaching. soldiers killed them, with Elba and Celina Ramos, in their house on the campus.

practice: Bring to mind a teacher who mattered to you, then widen the circle to anyone, right now, who tells the truth where that's dangerous: teachers, journalists, students. Hold them, and Elba and Celina too, for a few slow breaths.
If you pray, pray for their safety and courage, or say today's names one by one; if not, simply keep them in mind with respect.

wordCard.voice: The Salvadoran Jesuits. Six priests and two women killed at their university in San Salvador, remembered for teaching the truth about the poor during a war. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: killed for teaching. Elba and Celina belong in the story too. Go gently.
